title: Umm Salamah
hookLine: her counsel breaks a silence at Hudaybiyyah, and her question is answered by a verse of the Qur'an

lines: A TREATY THAT FEELS LIKE DEFEAT.
HE GOES IN TO HIS WIFE.
cards: Nobody moves. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has just agreed a treaty at Hudaybiyyah, outside Mecca, and the terms feel to his companions like a defeat.
He tells them: get up, sacrifice your animals, and shave your heads. Bukhari says not one of them rose. He says it again.
And again. Silence. So he goes into his tent, to his wife, and tells her what has happened.

teach.b: Her advice, in Bukhari, is short and wise. Go out, she says, and don't say a word to anyone. Sacrifice your own animal, and call your barber to shave your head.
And when the companions see it, they get up, sacrifice, and start shaving one another, crowding so hard in their distress that it looked as if they might hurt each other.

Umm Salamah understood something about grief and pride: people who won't be argued into moving can sometimes be shown. That's the first thing she's remembered for: counsel in a hard hour. The second is a question.
In a report in the Musnad of Ahmad, Umm Salamah asks the Prophet: why are we, the women, not mentioned in the Qur'an the way the men are? She doesn't say it in a corner; she asks him directly.

And then, the report says, she heard him reciting from the pulpit a new verse, surah thirty-three, verse thirty-five. In Pickthall it begins: "Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender".

teach.h: MEN WHO SURRENDER, AND WOMEN WHO SURRENDER.
teach.b: It goes on like that, pair after pair: men who believe and women who believe, men who are truthful and women who are truthful, men who give charity and women who give charity, men who fast and women who fast, all the way to forgiveness and a vast reward.
The verse speaks to women and men alike.
The report adds a story behind it: someone asked. Her question didn't ask for less from women. It asked to be named.

how: Muslims recite surah 33:35 as a verse naming believing men and women side by side, and retell Umm Salamah's advice at Hudaybiyyah from Sahih al-Bukhari as an example of wise counsel.

o: the Prophet's foster mother in the desert
the wife who kept the Qur'an's pages
the wife whose counsel moved the silent camp

p: men and women named side by side

s: the companions obeyed at once at Hudaybiyyah
Bukhari says none rose though he told them three times.
Umm Salamah advised him to act without speaking
she told him to sacrifice and shave, saying nothing, and they followed.
Umm Salamah asked why women weren't mentioned like the men
the report in Ahmad links her question to surah 33:35.

games.q: you are the Prophet's wife. he tells you his companions won't move after the treaty, though he asked three times. what do you advise?
o: tell him to command them again, more strongly.
tell him to say nothing, and sacrifice and shave himself.
tell him to wait a day until they calm down.
games.why: in Bukhari she says: go out, speak to no one, sacrifice and call your barber. when they saw him, they all did the same.

practice: Think of a room you're part of, a family, a team, a congregation, a class, and whether there's someone, or something, nobody ever mentions there. Let the question form, as plainly as Umm Salamah's, and just hold the words for now.
If you pray, bring that question to Allah, as she brought hers to the Prophet.

wordCard.voice: Umm Salamah. The mother of the believers whose counsel moved the silent camp at Hudaybiyyah, and whose question is linked to the verse that names women and men side by side. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'mother of Salamah', named after her son; her own name was Hind.

carryVoice: Your line: she asked, and it came. One plain question, and a verse that names women and men side by side. Day eight hundred eleven.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (Hudaybiyyah; none rose; Umm Salamah's advice)
Musnad Ahmad 26575 (Umm Salamah asks why women are not mentioned; 33:35 recited from the pulpit)

sources.q: Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender
